title: Rabbi Yehudah bar Grogerot
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Yoma 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.78a), Yehudah bar Grogerot taught: “It is forbidden to sit on clay on Yom Kippur.” Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: “[This refers] to damp clay.” Tosafot Yeshanim there reads “Yehudah Grogerot,” explaining that this was his name. He is also mentioned in [Shabbat 108b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.108b) according to the Arukh’s reading, whereas our reading is “R. Y. bar Chaviva.” In Shekalim, chapter 4: “Rabbi Chizkiyah said: Rabbi Yehudah Grogerot taught.”[^1]

notes.text: The heading’s bar is retained rather than substituted with the catalog’s ben. ארי״בל is read contextually as “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said.” טינא מטפחת describes damp clay; מטפחת is not taken here as the noun “a cloth,” which made the earlier English fragment incoherent. The supplied words “[This refers]” make the terse qualification readable without adding a new ruling. The separate initials ר״י before bar Chaviva remain unresolved. Hyman’s full Shekalim locator is פ״ד ה״כ״ד:; no modern halakhah number is inferred from that compressed form. The Yoma/Shabbat locators עח. and קח: are conventionally 78a and 108b. No independent witness was supplied for the readings attributed to Tosafot Yeshanim or the Arukh.
